summary.text: A 36-year-old woman in the 11th week of her first pregnancy was referred for new-onset hyperthyroidism. She had multiple sclerosis diagnosed at age 27, treated with three courses of alemtuzumab, a positive family history of thyroid disorders and no smoking. She reported fine distal tremors, had a heart rate of 120 beats per minute, normal blood pressure and no active ophthalmopathy.

Free T4 was increased, TSH suppressed and TRAb 20.6 IU/L, with negative TPOAb and TgAb; thyroid ultrasound showed a normal-sized gland with heterogeneous, pseudonodular echotexture and increased uniform vascularization. Graves’ disease was diagnosed at 11 weeks of gestation, described as alemtuzumab-induced, and TRAb stayed persistently elevated through pregnancy.

Methimazole 10 mg/day was started and adjusted during pregnancy to 15, 12.5, 10 and 7.5 mg to maintain euthyroidism, with thyroid function tests every 2 to 3 weeks. Fetal growth was normal without signs of fetal hyperthyroidism, and she delivered a baby girl of 3610 g with a normal Apgar score and no obstetric complications.

The infant was euthyroid at 3 days with high-titer TRAb, developed transient neonatal hyperthyroidism at 10 days, was admitted with normal ultrasound, examination, electrocardiography and growth, needed no antithyroid therapy and recovered spontaneously. Mother and child were closely monitored postpartum, and at seven months postpartum she was euthyroid on methimazole 15 mg/day without signs of MS relapse; the sources conflict on whether her dose was increased or tapered.
